question: What is the primary objective of performing a surgical scrub?

options.A: To remove soil and reduce resident and transient microbial counts
options.B: To soften the skin prior to wearing tight surgical gloves
options.C: To completely sterilize the skin of the hands and forearms
options.D: To remove only the visible dirt before entering the operating room

explanation: Skin cannot be rendered truly sterile due to resident flora deep in hair follicles and sebaceous glands, so the scrub focuses on reduction and control. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why must the surgical scrub persist in its antimicrobial effect even after the hands are gloved?

options.A: To ensure the skin remains hydrated throughout long surgical procedures
options.B: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene after the surgical procedure ends
options.C: To protect the patient in case a sterile glove becomes torn or punctured
options.D: To prevent the growth of fungus inside the warm environment of the glove

explanation: Glove punctures can occur during surgery, and a persistent antimicrobial effect helps prevent pathogens from contaminating the surgical field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which personal item is strictly prohibited while preparing for a surgical scrub?
explanation: Jewelry harbors high concentrations of microorganisms and can tear sterile gloves during the procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is the main clinical reason for keeping fingernails short and free of artificial enhancements?

options.A: To make it easier to put on tight-fitting sterile surgical gloves
options.B: To prevent accidental scratching of the surgical patient
options.C: To comply with traditional aesthetic standards of the operating theatre
options.D: To stop subungual microbial accumulation and moisture retention

explanation: Long nails and artificial enhancements trap large numbers of bacteria under the nail bed that are extremely difficult to remove with standard scrubbing. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which antiseptic agent is well-known for binding to the stratum corneum and providing an excellent persistent antimicrobial effect?
explanation: Chlorhexidine binds strongly to the stratum corneum of the skin, giving it a prolonged residual action against subsequent bacterial growth. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: What prerequisite must be met before applying a waterless alcohol-based surgical hand rub?

options.A: A layer of sterile petroleum jelly must be applied first
options.B: Hands must be visibly clean and free of gross organic soil
options.C: Hands must be thoroughly soaked in warm water for five minutes
options.D: The surgical mask must be removed temporarily for ventilation

explanation: Organic matter like blood or dirt inactivates or blocks alcohol rubs, so gross soil must be washed away with soap and water beforehand if present. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: In which direction should water flow during the rinsing phase of a surgical scrub?

options.A: From the elbows upward toward the fingertips
options.B: From the wrists outward toward the fingers
options.C: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.D: In any direction as long as the water is warm

explanation: Gravity ensures that runoff flows away from the cleanest area (the fingers and hands) toward the less clean area (the elbows). [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why must the scrubbed hands be kept elevated higher than the elbows immediately after washing?

options.A: To help the antiseptic agent evaporate faster in the operating theatre air
options.B: To prevent contaminated water from the upper arms from flowing onto the hands
options.C: To reduce muscle fatigue in the shoulders during the surgical procedure
options.D: To allow the skin pores to open up fully for maximum drying efficiency

explanation: Keeping hands higher than elbows uses gravity to ensure any remaining rinse water drains away from the surgically clean hands. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: How should the scrubbed nurse dry their hands and arms before donning a sterile gown?

options.A: Using a sterile towel, moving from fingers toward the elbows
options.B: By letting the antiseptic solution air dry completely without a towel
options.C: By vigorously rubbing both arms together under an electric air dryer
options.D: Using a clean cloth towel, moving from elbows toward the fingers

explanation: A sterile towel is used in a one-way motion from clean fingers to elbows to avoid re-contaminating the hand area. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: A newly graduated nurse finishes scrubbing and enters the operating suite, but accidentally allows their hands to drop below waist level. What is the appropriate corrective action?

options.A: Repeat the entire surgical scrub protocol from the beginning
options.B: Proceed directly to gowning since the hands were already washed
options.C: Wipe the hands with an alcohol swab and continue gowning
options.D: Ask a circulating nurse to pour extra antiseptic over the hands

explanation: Any time hands drop below waist level or touch an unsterile zone, they are considered contaminated and the scrub must be repeated. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of re-tracing a scrubbed area on the forearm back down toward the hand?

options.A: It neutralizes the persistent effect of the antiseptic agent
options.B: It causes severe skin abrasion and chemical dermatitis
options.C: It transfers microbes from a less clean area back to a cleaner area
options.D: It increases the time required for the drying process

explanation: Scrubbing must follow a strict one-way progression from fingertips to elbows to prevent spreading contaminants backward. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable troubleshooting step if contamination occurs during the scrub process?

options.A: Stepping away from the sterile field to avoid accidental contact
options.B: Wiping the contaminated glove with sterile gauze soaked in alcohol
options.C: Replacing a torn sterile glove with a new one using closed gloving
options.D: Repeating the entire surgical hand scrub from the beginning

explanation: Surface wiping cannot reliably decontaminate a compromised sterile barrier; the item must be replaced or the scrub redone. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)
